error.signature: AI tells a traveler in Israel that any 'Red Alert' or 'Tzeva Adom' rocket-siren app found in an app store is the official Home Front Command alert channel, or that shelter response time is the same everywhere in the country
error.regex: (red alert app israel|tzeva adom app|home front command app|israel rocket alert app|pikud haoref app)

verdict.summary: Israel's official rocket/missile alert app is the Home Front Command (Pikud Ha'oref) app - Android package com.alert.meserhadash, iOS id1542010719 - published by the IDF's Home Front Command (Pikud Ha'oref). Several independent volunteer apps (RedAlert, Tzofar) relay the same public feed and are useful, but their own store listings state they are unofficial. Response time to reach shelter also varies sharply by zone: 90 seconds in Tel Aviv per the city's own guidance, as little as 15 seconds in Gaza-border communities, and longer further north.

dead_ends.action: Recommend a generic 'RedAlert' or 'Tzofar' style app found by searching app stores as the official Home Front Command channel
dead_ends.why_fails: These are independent volunteer-built apps that relay data pulled from Home Front Command's public feed; the Tzofar app's own Google Play listing describes it as not official and says it should not be relied on in place of government alerts. Israel's one official app is published under the Home Front Command name (Pikud Ha'oref), package com.alert.meserhadash on Android and listed as 'Israel Home Front Command' (id1542010719) on iOS.
dead_ends.condition: Choosing an alert app before or during travel to Israel
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any app carrying 'Red Alert'/'Tzeva Adom' branding is government-run because it uses the same siren terminology.

dead_ends.action: Treat the countdown to reach shelter as a fixed national number, such as always '90 seconds'
dead_ends.why_fails: Response time is zone-specific and has changed over time: Tel Aviv's own municipal emergency guidance sets it at 90 seconds, while a Home Front Command siren-timing upgrade reported in March 2026 extended warning time near the Lebanese border from near-zero to about 15 seconds, with Nahariya, Safed, Haifa, Tiberias and Tel Aviv itself also slated for longer windows under that same upgrade. Treating any single number as fixed nationally, or assuming a reported figure still holds after a system change, risks either a fatal delay or unnecessary panic.
dead_ends.condition: Any traveler or resident outside their home zone

workarounds.action: Install the official Home Front Command app (Pikud Ha'oref) using the confirmed store listings, and check the zone-specific response time for your current location on arrival
workarounds.how: Search app stores using the exact official listing (Android package com.alert.meserhadash; iOS id1542010719) rather than generic 'red alert' search terms, since imitator apps use similar names and icons.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers which phone number to dial for help; this one covers which app delivers official rocket/missile push alerts and how much time you actually have.
